To create a Python function that returns the uppercase version of a given text, you can use the `.upper()` method of string objects. Below is a simple function that takes a string as an input and returns it in uppercase:

```python
def to_upper(text):
    return text.upper()

# Example usage
input_text = "Hello, World!"
output_text = to_upper(input_text)
print(output_text)  # Output will be: HELLO, WORLD!
```

This function `to_upper` will convert all lowercase letters in the input string to their uppercase counterparts. If the input text already includes uppercase letters or non-alphabetic characters, they will remain unchanged in the output.
